items.note: One-group pre-post quasi-experiment: 28 EFL student teachers taught descriptive and narrative writing with ChatGPT, Jenni and Whimsical; rubric scores fluency, accuracy and originality; no comparison group and below 50 participants.

Two field experiments on LLM use in job-application cover letters; outcome is signal quality of the letters and interview invitations, not creativity; diversity (standardization) only implicit; listed as accepted at JOLE, abstract from Crossref SSRN record.

Field study with 75 children aged 9-10 assigned to curious question-asking training with hand-made closed cues, GPT-3 closed cues, or GPT-3 open cues; divergent questions annotated by humans; children do not use the AI directly (AI generates training content), so the next stage should check whether this counts as AI assistance.

User study of essay writing with varying LLM use (heavy users wrote more neutral essays; creativity only self-reported), plus model-only LLM revisions of 2021 essays and an observational analysis of AI-written peer reviews; whether LLM use was assigned or chosen is not stated, and the search notes' N of 100 is unverified.

Arabic-language article: three intact tenth-grade classes (25 each) allocated at random to classroom training, AI-tool-based training, or control; Torrance Test (fluency, flexibility, originality) pre, post and follow-up; class-level allocation of three clusters, not individual randomization; outcome is unassisted creativity after training (after_ai).

Mixed-methods study with 80 EFL undergraduates in GenAI and control groups; creative writing scored for originality and structural academic writing assessed with t-tests and MANOVA; abstract read from the journal landing page (DOI not resolvable in Crossref/OpenAlex); assignment method unclear.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC empty; Springer page blocked; web search found only the citation); classified as experiment only by the doubt rule, design could be a survey or qualitative study, check full text.

2x2 RCT with 1,053 Bocconi first-years crossing ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access with causal-reasoning training on a merchandising business problem; expert rubric scores, number of ideas and idea diversity; abstract from RePEc; also released as an OpenAI report PDF.

Lab experiment randomly assigning participants to ChatGPT access or not in an open-ended creative writing task, with Prolific raters scoring creative performance and incentive schemes varied; N not in abstract (search notes say 360); same work as the Ca' Foscari DSE WP 16/2026.

18 students wrote essays with (n=9) or without (n=9) ChatGPT-3.5; essay grades, writing time, authenticity and between-essay similarity measured; below 50 participants; same study as arXiv 2302.04536 and EdArXiv preprint.
